+---
+author: Nic Patterson (nic@reynn.dev)
+state: not started
+---
+
+# API Server Design Document
+
+## What
+
+The Job Processor API server manages job requests from end user CLIs.
+
+## Why
+
+The API server is designed to allow many users to submit jobs to a central system and retrieve the job output as needed.
+A typical use case is a team of developers can deploy the API server to a machine hosted in a restricted VPC, they can then install tools and other necessities and submit jobs from their local machine.
+Any command that can be run on a Linux based machine can be sent to the API server to be processed, if the command is not available the job will fail immediately, this will have the job go directly from `queued` to `failed`.
+
+## Details
+
+### Persistence
+
+In this initial version job metadata will be stored in a `sync.Map` with a randomly assigned UUID is used as the key and the job struct as the value.
+This means when the API server is shut down or restarted all metadata is lost.
+In a fully fleshed out application this information would be persisted to some kind of database such as PostgreSQL, Redis, AWS DynamoDB or other similar data store.
+
+### Job
+
+```go
+// Job A job is a Linux command
+type Job struct {
+  ID             string
+  ProcessID      int
+  Command        string
+  Args           []string
+  Status         JobStatus
+  CombinedOutput []byte

@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+---
+author: Nic Patterson (nic@reynn.dev)
+state: not started
+---
+
+# grpc-job-processor Design Document
+
+## What
+
+This project provides a gRPC API server that allows a user to process Linux jobs.
+A client will be able to start, stop, pause and get the status of a job.
+
+### Goals
+
+- Go library that handles start/stop/status actions of a job.
+- gRPC API server that will process jobs asynchronously.
+- Resource control (CPU/Memory/Disk IO) via cgroups for processed jobs.
+- CLI client to send jobs to a server.
+- mTLS authentication between CLI and API.
+
+## Why
+
+Sometimes a user needs to run a Linux command on a potentially remote machine so their terminal isn't blocked by the running process.
+This project aims to allow a team of users to submit Linux jobs to a shared system and monitor the job until it completes.
+
+## Details
+
+This project is broken into 3 major pieces; an library, a gRPC API server that receives and processes jobs, and a CLI client used to send and monitor jobs from a user terminal.
+
+### Library
+
+#### Library: Jobs
+
+Package handling the actually starting and stopping of a job process.
+
+#### Library: CGroups
+
+Package handles launching a process into a cgroup, only a subset of cgroupv2 features are supported with the initial version of the package.
comment.body: Could you elaborate on how jobs will be spawned in cgroups and what your cgroup hierarchy will look like?

@@ -0,0 +1,85 @@
+---
+author: Nic Patterson (nic@reynn.dev)
+state: not started
+---
+
+# API Server Design Document
+
+## What
+
+The Job Processor API server manages job requests from end user CLIs.
+
+## Why
+
+The API server is designed to allow many users to submit jobs to a central system and retrieve the job output as needed.
+A typical use case is a team of developers can deploy the API server to a machine hosted in a restricted VPC, they can then install tools and other necessities and submit jobs from their local machine.
+Any command that can be run on a Linux based machine can be sent to the API server to be processed, if the command is not available the job will fail immediately.
+
+## Details
+
+### Launch Flags
+
+Used to modify the application settings before startup.
+
+| Flag | Description                                         |
+| ---- | --------------------------------------------------- |
+| -w   | Number of Job Processor workers (default: numcpu-1) |
+| -p   | Port to start the server on (default: 50051)        |
+
+### Persistence
+
+In this initial version job metadata will be stored in a `sync.Map` with the randomly assigned ID is used as the key and the job struct as the value.
+This means when the API server is shut down or restarted all metadata is lost.
+In a fully fleshed out application this information would be persisted to some kind of database such as PostgreSQL, Redis, AWS DynamoDB or other similar data store.
+
+### Job
+
+```go
+// Job A job is a Linux command
+type Job struct {
+  ID        string
+  ProcessID int
+  Command   string
+  Args      []string
+  Status    JobStatus
+  Output    []byte
+  ExitCode  int
+  Error     string
+}
+```
+
+### Job Statuses
+
+```go
+type JobStatus string
+
+const (
+  JobStatusQueued    JobStatus = "queued"
+  JobStatusStarted   JobStatus = "started"
+  JobStatusStopped   JobStatus = "stopped"
+  JobStatusCompleted JobStatus = "completed"
+  JobStatusFailed    JobStatus = "failed"
+)
+```
+
+A job has a specific status assigned so you can determine the state of a job.
+A `queued` job can only go to the `started` state. A `started` job can go to one of `stopped`, `completed` or `failed` based on what happens during execution.
+
+| status    | description                                                      |
+| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| queued    | A job that has been submitted but has not yet started processing |
+| started   | Job has been started but has not completed yet                   |
+| stopped   | Job has been manually stopped by a user                          |
+| completed | Job has completed successfully                                   |
+| failed    | Job has failed to complete, the exit code should be available    |
+
+### Job Processor
+
+The job processor will handle the starting/stopping of jobs that have been submitted to the API.
+The processor will have `n` number of worker routines that will each take a submitted job and stay attached until the job completes.
+Number of worker routines will default to number of CPU cores minus 1 (minimum of 2 workers), it can be configured using the `-w` flag when starting the API server.
+
+### Authentication/Authorization
+
+Authentication is provided via a basic mTLS certificate controller. Once a user has successfully authenticated they are authorized to view jobs that are either public or that they started.
comment.body: Could you elaborate a little more? How is the authentication information going to be used by the authorization layer? How are users identified?

+### Job Processor
+
+The job processor will handle the starting/stopping of jobs that have been submitted to the API.
+The processor will have `n` number of worker routines that will each take a submitted job and stay attached until the job completes.
comment.body: Not in the specs, just spawn jobs and goroutines as needed by clients.
